description: Structured scope-gap tracking for the three recurring interview feedback themes.

scope_dimensions.label: ERP Leadership Breadth
scope_dimensions.employer_concern: Can this person lead an enterprise-wide system landscape, integrations, governance, and change across multiple platforms/business units?
scope_dimensions.amber_evidence: SAP S/4HANA ownership including RISE/UAT/hypercare, BDC/LSMW, governed mass-change delivery, 2,167-FLOC-BOM production migration; enterprise master-data governance across 40K+ assets and 11K+ maintenance plans; cross-functional transformation leadership; ServiceNow intake/governance; training/adoption and executive stakeholder translation.
scope_dimensions.risk: Deep SAP PM/MM/MDM and S/4HANA data governance experience but has not owned a full enterprise ERP portfolio across all modules (FI/CO/SD/PP/MM/HR) in a formal portfolio-leadership capacity.
scope_dimensions.interview_bridge: 90-second ERP leadership story: scope of systems owned, governance framework built, cross-functional teams led, measurable outcomes. Broader ERP portfolio scope is the next logical extension of work already being done.

scope_dimensions.label: Direct Procurement Experience
scope_dimensions.employer_concern: Can this person make sourcing, supplier, spend, contract, and stakeholder trade-offs with direct ownership?
scope_dimensions.amber_evidence: Sumitomo production planning with forecasts-to-POs, supplier readiness coordination, international shipment tracking, inventory exposure; CSL supplier coordination, vendor performance management, ASN uploads; procurement-adjacent governance: spend analysis, vendor data governance, contract/renewal support.
scope_dimensions.risk: Has procurement-adjacent and supply-chain procurement experience but has not held formal end-to-end category management, strategic sourcing, or direct procurement leadership ownership.
scope_dimensions.interview_bridge: Procurement-adjacent story: specific vendor/category decisions, operational requirements defined, service/risk trade-offs evaluated, cost savings achieved. Operator's perspective that sourcing decisions must survive implementation.

scope_dimensions.label: $10M Technology Budget Ownership
scope_dimensions.employer_concern: Can this person prioritize investments, manage run-vs-change spend, defend trade-offs, and forecast accurately at $10M+ scale?
scope_dimensions.amber_evidence: Governed vendor spend and project portfolios; business-case development; cost avoidance through automation; portfolio prioritization decisions; executive communication of trade-offs; forecasting and budget input for data/technology initiatives.
scope_dimensions.risk: Has budget influence and management experience but has not held sole formal cost-center ownership of a $10M technology-tower budget.
scope_dimensions.interview_bridge: Financial-governance story: actual spend influenced, vendor economics managed, business cases built, prioritization decisions made, trade-offs communicated to leadership. Scale is the development step, not the type of work.

per_role_assessment.title: Senior Manager, ERP Platform

erp_breadth.evidence: SAP S/4HANA data governance and migration; cross-functional ERP transformation leadership

direct_procurement.evidence: Role focused on ERP platform, not procurement

budget_ownership.evidence: Role scope unclear on budget ownership

per_role_assessment.outcome: Rejected after HR screen + Hiring Manager/Director of IT interview
per_role_assessment.feedback_theme: Scope concern — employer likely sought candidate with formal enterprise ERP platform ownership breadth

per_role_assessment.title: Manager, Procurement Digitalization

erp_breadth.evidence: No ERP concern raised in this interview. Focus was on procurement knowledge and digitalization roadmap.

direct_procurement.evidence: Hiring manager explicitly stated: "having an understanding of procurement is probably core to it... that's the only gap that I see at this point." This is a direct quote from the transcript.

budget_ownership.evidence: Not directly discussed in this interview. Hiring manager mentioned the role involves building business cases and selling them to upper management for funding approval.

per_role_assessment.outcome: Pending — first-round interview completed. Hiring manager said Lacey will be in touch about next steps.
per_role_assessment.feedback_theme: Procurement understanding is the single explicit gap identified. Hiring manager was otherwise positive. Role requires strategic technology decision (system expiring in 1.5 years) and PeopleSoft→SAP migration support.

per_role_assessment.title: Manager, Supply Chain Technology & Operations

erp_breadth.requirement: Supply chain technology and ERP systems
erp_breadth.evidence: Panel confirmed SAP experience is strong (plant maintenance + materials management modules). Justin Slater (Director, Production IT) engaged on Springfield paint shop automation. No ERP concern raised.

direct_procurement.evidence: Harshan (Procurement & Supply Quality Manager) asked about procurement IT integration points. Amber could describe source-to-contract and supplier/contract interfaces but from research, not direct experience.

budget_ownership.evidence: Justin Slater directly questioned: "What do you think would be your biggest challenge with managing a multimillion dollar budget?" Amber's current $60K budget only covers merit increases and bonuses for 5 direct reports. She does not own capital or operating budgets. This is a confirmed gap from the transcript.

per_role_assessment.outcome: Pending — first-round panel interview completed. Still interviewing other candidates.
per_role_assessment.feedback_theme: Budget ownership is the primary concern. Panel probed financial responsibility depth. Procurement system knowledge is secondary concern. SAP and compliance experience are strengths.

per_role_assessment.title: Sr. Production Planning Data Analyst

erp_breadth.evidence: SAP master data governance, Power BI, analytics

per_role_assessment.outcome: Interview requested, screen cancelled — role filled by another candidate
per_role_assessment.feedback_theme: No feedback received — employer filled position before interview

pattern_summary: Both International Motors interviews confirm the three feedback themes from actual transcripts. The Procurement Digitalization hiring manager explicitly stated procurement understanding is "the only gap" (direct quote). The Supply Chain Manager panel (Major Ramirez, Harshan, Justin Slater) directly questioned Amber's budget ownership — her $60K budget only covers merit/bonus for 5 reports, not capital or operating budgets. Justin Slater asked about managing a "multimillion dollar budget." SAP/ERP experience was confirmed as a strength in both interviews. Both roles are still pending — International Motors is completing first-round interviews "this week and next week." Combined Metals advanced Amber to the hiring-manager stage before rejection. The pattern is consistent: ERP breadth is a strength, but direct procurement experience and budget ownership scope are the two gaps that interviewers consistently probe. Amber should prepare targeted responses for both before any future interviews.
